Research task for Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, staging tree at /opt/nxeon-staging for any lookups). No code changes — pure research/report.

First, check `lib/games.ts` at /opt/nxeon-staging for the full existing game catalog (already has ~30 entries after recent additions) to confirm none of these 5 are already present before researching them as "new" candidates.

Research these 5 games for addability to Nxeon's game-hosting catalog, using the same bar as previous research passes: real official (or at minimum broadly legitimate) dedicated server support, a beatable (peer-tier, not mega-authority) hosting SERP, and — since "no GPUs yet" is a hard constraint — no GPU dependency.

1. **World of Warcraft (private servers)** — this is legally the most sensitive one, similar in shape to the Call of Duty/Plutonium research done earlier (an active, actively-monetized Blizzard MMO with unofficial private-server emulation, e.g. TrinityCore/CMaNGOS-based projects). Blizzard has a well-documented history of aggressive enforcement (Nostalrius' 2016 shutdown after a huge player petition is the classic case), but some projects (Warmane, others) have operated for over a decade. Research: current 2026 legal/enforcement landscape specifically for WoW private servers, whether any hosting companies currently sell "WoW private server hosting" openly (and how they frame/brand it), how big the demand signal is, and what technical requirements exist (emulator core, database, client-side patching needed by players). Produce the same kind of structured risk assessment as the Plutonium research (Landscape / Competitors / Technical / Demand / Risk mitigation) since this is likely an even higher-risk call than CoD.

2. **Team Fortress 2** — official Valve dedicated server via SteamCMD, very mature. Confirm current dedicated-server support still works normally (no recent Valve policy changes), check SERP for "TF2 server hosting" / "Team Fortress 2 dedicated server" (established peer-tier hosts expected — confirm who: Shockbyte, Nodecraft, GTX Gaming, etc. — assess beatability), and note current player-base/demand health (TF2 had a major "Bot Crisis" a few years back — check if that's been resolved and the game is healthy enough to be worth hosting).

3. **DayZ** — official Bohemia Interactive dedicated server via SteamCMD, widely hosted already industry-wide. Confirm and check SERP beatability the same way.

4. **PUBG: Battlegrounds** — this one has a messier history: PUBG Corp/Krafton's "Community Servers" program has historically been partnership-gated/whitelisted rather than open public SteamCMD hosting like Source-engine games. Research the CURRENT (2026) state: is there any legitimate path for a hosting company like Nxeon to offer real PUBG dedicated servers to customers today, or does it remain locked to Krafton-approved partners only? Be precise here — don't assume it works like other games.

5. **Left 4 Dead 2** (and note if original Left 4 Dead is meaningfully different/relevant — likely just cover L4D2 as the modern one) — official Valve dedicated server via SteamCMD, very mature, similar maturity to TF2. Same SERP/demand check.

For each, conclude clearly: ADD (clean, low risk, real demand) / ADD WITH CAUTION (works but has a flag worth the owner knowing) / DO NOT ADD (blocked — explain exactly why, e.g. no real public dedicated-server path, or legal risk assessed as too high).

Report back structured by game, under 700 words total (the WoW section can run a bit longer given its risk-assessment depth, similar treatment to the Plutonium report; the other 4 can be brief since they're much more standard).

/** Families whose OsTemplate rows are game servers. Plain module (safe to import
 *  from server components and "use server" action files alike). */
export const GAME_FAMILIES = ["minecraft", "valheim", "rust", "palworld", "cs2", "terraria", "ark", "satisfactory", "projectzomboid", "sdtd", "vrising", "enshrouded", "factorio", "gmod", "conan", "unturned", "theforest", "sonsoftheforest", "bedrock", "schedule1", "dragonwilds", "sunkenland", "abioticfactor", "corekeeper", "icarus"] as const;
export type GameFamily = (typeof GAME_FAMILIES)[number];

/**
 * Canonical display name + glyph per family, ALL 19 — the single source of truth
 * for capitalization (e.g. "Garry's Mod", "7 Days to Die", "ARK: Survival
 * Evolved", never a raw lowercase slug). Plain module, so unlike
 * components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx's GAME_VISUAL (which is "use client" and
 * also carries brand gradient colors) this is safe to import from a SERVER
 * component too.
 *
 * FIXED 2026-08-23: the deploy wizard's game picker (app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx)
 * and the "manage my servers" list (app/dashboard/games/page.tsx) each kept their
 * OWN copy-pasted map with only 6 of 19 games — every other family silently fell
 * back to its raw slug ("sdtd", "gmod", "theforest"...) with no capitalization at
 * all. Both now import this instead of maintaining their own list.
 */
export const GAME_DISPLAY: Record<GameFamily, { name: string; glyph: string }> = {
  minecraft: { name: "Minecraft", glyph: "⛏️" },
  valheim: { name: "Valheim", glyph: "🪓" },
  rust: { name: "Rust", glyph: "🔧" },
  palworld: { name: "Palworld", glyph: "🐾" },
  cs2: { name: "Counter-Strike 2", glyph: "🎯" },
  terraria: { name: "Terraria", glyph: "🌳" },
  ark: { name: "ARK: Survival Evolved", glyph: "🦖" },
  satisfactory: { name: "Satisfactory", glyph: "🏭" },
  projectzomboid: { name: "Project Zomboid", glyph: "🧟" },
  sdtd: { name: "7 Days to Die", glyph: "🪓" },
  vrising: { name: "V Rising", glyph: "🩸" },
  enshrouded: { name: "Enshrouded", glyph: "🌫️" },
  factorio: { name: "Factorio", glyph: "🏭" },
  gmod: { name: "Garry's Mod", glyph: "🧰" },
  conan: { name: "Conan Exiles", glyph: "🗡️" },
  unturned: { name: "Unturned", glyph: "🏝️" },
  theforest: { name: "The Forest", glyph: "🌲" },
  sonsoftheforest: { name: "Sons of the Forest", glyph: "🪚" },
  bedrock: { name: "Minecraft Bedrock", glyph: "🧱" },
  // ── Wave 3. dragonwilds/sunkenland/abioticfactor/corekeeper/icarus made orderable
  //    2026-08-31 (prisma/seed-wave3-games.ts — GamePlan+OsTemplate seeded on staging).
  //    schedule1 stays SCAFFOLD ONLY: no official dedicated server exists (P2P/lobby),
  //    so it is deliberately NOT seeded — see lib/game-control.ts. ──
  schedule1: { name: "Schedule I", glyph: "💊" },
  dragonwilds: { name: "RuneScape: Dragonwilds", glyph: "🐉" },
  sunkenland: { name: "Sunkenland", glyph: "🌊" },
  abioticfactor: { name: "Abiotic Factor", glyph: "🧪" },
  corekeeper: { name: "Core Keeper", glyph: "🪨" },
  icarus: { name: "Icarus", glyph: "🚀" },
};

/**
 * Family id → art slug for the real key-art bundled at
 * public/games/art/<slug>_poster.jpg and public/games/art/<slug>_hero.jpg
 * (naming differs from the family id for a few titles). Single source of truth
 * for every consumer (GameCoverCarousel, GameCoverTile, GameHero) — was
 * previously copy-pasted separately in GameCoverCarousel.tsx, which is exactly
 * the kind of drift that caused the GAME_DISPLAY capitalization bug above.
 *
 * `poster` is omitted for minecraft (no poster art was provided — it resolves
 * real cover art via a different fallback chain instead). Every family has a
 * `hero`.
 */
/**
 * Family id → the port a customer's game client actually connects to, plus
 * which transport it is reachable on. This is the single source of truth for
 * `worker/provision-health.ts`'s post-boot game-port verification (added after
 * a Terraria order silently sat on an interactive world-selection prompt with
 * no TTY — the container showed "Up" while nothing ever bound the port, and
 * PROVISION reported success anyway).
 *
 * SOURCED DIRECTLY from each family's `docker run -p ...` mapping in
 * prisma/catalog.ts / prisma/seed-wave1-games.ts / prisma/seed-wave2-games.ts —
 * these are the ONLY ports Docker actually exposes off the container, so they
 * are the only ports reachable from outside it. If a game's setup script ever
 * changes its `-p` mapping, this entry must change with it or the health check
 * will probe a port nothing forwards to.
 *
 * `protocol` is not always the game's own play port: several titles (valheim,
 * palworld, vrising, enshrouded, theforest, sonsoftheforest, bedrock) expose
 * ONLY a UDP port in their image — no TCP port is mapped at all, so there is
 * nothing a TCP connect could ever prove for them. Where an image also exposes
 * a TCP port (often RCON/query, e.g. rust's 28016, ark's 27020, factorio's
 * 27015) THAT port is used instead: a TCP handshake is verifiable with a plain
 * connect, and the process binding it is proof the game server itself came up,
 * which is exactly the class of bug this check exists to catch — even though
 * it isn't the port the player's game client uses to join.
 */
export const GAME_PORT: Record<GameFamily, { port: number; protocol: "tcp" | "udp" }> = {
  minecraft: { port: 25565, protocol: "tcp" },
  valheim: { port: 2456, protocol: "udp" }, // no tcp port mapped
  rust: { port: 28016, protocol: "tcp" }, // rcon tcp; 28015/udp is the join port
  palworld: { port: 8211, protocol: "udp" }, // no tcp port mapped
  cs2: { port: 27015, protocol: "tcp" },
  terraria: { port: 7777, protocol: "tcp" },
  ark: { port: 27020, protocol: "tcp" }, // rcon tcp; 7777/7778/27015 are udp
  satisfactory: { port: 7777, protocol: "tcp" }, // image maps 7777 as both tcp+udp
  projectzomboid: { port: 27015, protocol: "tcp" }, // rcon tcp; 16261/16262 are udp
  sdtd: { port: 26900, protocol: "tcp" }, // 26900 is mapped as both tcp+udp
  vrising: { port: 9876, protocol: "udp" }, // no tcp port mapped
  enshrouded: { port: 15636, protocol: "udp" }, // no tcp port mapped
  factorio: { port: 27015, protocol: "tcp" }, // rcon tcp; 34197/udp is the join port
  gmod: { port: 27015, protocol: "tcp" },
  conan: { port: 7777, protocol: "tcp" }, // image maps 7777 as both tcp+udp
  unturned: { port: 27015, protocol: "tcp" }, // 27015-27017 mapped as both tcp+udp
  theforest: { port: 27015, protocol: "udp" }, // no tcp port mapped
  sonsoftheforest: { port: 8766, protocol: "udp" }, // no tcp port mapped
  bedrock: { port: 19132, protocol: "udp" }, // RakNet — no tcp variant exists
  // ── Wave 3. dragonwilds/sunkenland/abioticfactor/corekeeper/icarus ports below are
  //    CONFIRMED against the real `-p ...` mapping in prisma/seed-wave3-games.ts
  //    (2026-08-31) — all four Wine-based/native images map UDP-only, so the health
  //    check probes the UDP game port. schedule1 stays unseeded (see below). ──
  schedule1: { port: 38465, protocol: "tcp" }, // UNVERIFIED: no official dedicated server exists (P2P/lobby) — stays unseeded
  dragonwilds: { port: 7777, protocol: "udp" }, // RS:Dragonwilds default game port (7778 = secondary)

## Catalog check

Confirmed against `/opt/nxeon-staging/lib/games.ts`: none of the 5 candidates (WoW private servers, TF2, DayZ, PUBG, L4D2) exist in the current 30-entry `GAME_FAMILIES` list. All are genuinely new.

## 1. World of Warcraft (private servers) — DO NOT ADD

**Landscape:** Not legal — private servers run unlicensed Blizzard IP via emulator cores (TrinityCore, CMaNGOS, AzerothCore) against ripped client data. Grey-area framing by fan sites doesn't change the underlying copyright exposure.

**2026 enforcement is escalating, not stable.** Blizzard filed suit against Turtle WoW (Aug 2025) and won in April 2026; Turtle WoW shut down 14 May 2026 after ~8 years of operation, and Stormforge shut down the same week under a cease-and-desist. This is the opposite of the Nostalrius pattern the task cites — it shows even long-lived, "safe-seeming" projects (8+ years) got taken down in the last few months. The lawsuit reportedly included racketeering claims, not just copyright/trademark — a sign Blizzard is going after the money layer, which is exactly where a hosting company selling "WoW private server hosting" would sit.

**Competitors:** Warmane and similar large servers survive mainly by operating outside US/EU jurisdiction with anonymized ownership — a posture Nxeon (a real, named, US/EU-reachable business) cannot replicate. `HostBarrel` was the only company found openly selling "WoW private server hosting"; it's a small, low-authority niche operator, not a peer-tier SERP with an established playbook to copy.

**Technical:** Requires an emulator core + MySQL DB + serving/hosting modified client data — meaningfully more legally-loaded than "run a Docker image" since Nxeon would be distributing/hosting altered game assets, not just a server binary.

**Demand:** Real (large private-server communities exist), but the risk-adjusted math is bad: this is a live-monetized MMO whose IP holder is actively suing and winning in 2026, with the clearest example of enforcement reaching a decade-old project within this same year. Verdict: **DO NOT ADD** — legal risk assessed as too high, similar to or exceeding the CoD/Plutonium call, and the "no GPU" constraint isn't even the blocker here — the business/legal exposure is.

## 2. Team Fortress 2 — ADD

Official Valve dedicated server via SteamCMD works normally, no policy changes. TF2's 2023-24 "bot crisis" is substantially resolved — Valve ran a bot-banwave and player count reportedly doubled afterward; residual bot activity exists but the game is healthy again, and 2026 hosting guides are current. SERP is peer-tier and beatable: Shockbyte ($9.99/mo), Nodecraft (~$10/mo), GTX Gaming ($6.40/mo) — established but same class of competitor Nxeon already competes against for CS2/GMod. No GPU dependency (Source engine, CPU-only). Clean addition.

## 3. DayZ — ADD

Official Bohemia Interactive dedicated server, Linux-supported directly per BI's own wiki, SteamCMD-installable (app 223350, note: requires a Steam account owning DayZ — anonymous login doesn't work, a minor provisioning detail not a blocker). Server performance improved notably in 2026 (BI cites a 9→50 server-FPS fix in the 1.29 cycle). RAM needs scale with mods (6GB floor, 12-16GB for heavy modded/60+ pop) but no GPU. SERP is the standard, beatable game-hosting-industry crowd (XGamingServer, gameserver.rentals, etc.) — same competitive tier as Nxeon's existing survival titles. Clean addition.

## 4. PUBG: Battlegrounds — DO NOT ADD

This is the one where the premise doesn't hold. PUBG has **no open public dedicated-server/SteamCMD path** for third parties — confirmed for 2026: Krafton's official position is that PUBG does not officially support community-hosted servers; what exists instead are partner-gated custom game modes/Sandbox Mode for approved content creators and esports orgs (`partnerhub.pubg.com`), not a purchasable dedicated-server binary. Multiple "PUBG server hosting" sites do appear in search results, but they are selling either misleading listings or generic cloud VMs marketed as "PUBG hosting" without a real, functioning dedicated-server product behind them — several adjacent reviews flag outright scam-pattern hosts in this niche. Verdict: **DO NOT ADD** — no legitimate technical path exists for Nxeon to deliver a real product here; selling it would mean shipping something that doesn't actually work as advertised.

## 5. Left 4 Dead 2 — ADD

Official Valve dedicated server via SteamCMD (app 222860), same maturity tier as TF2; 2026 guides confirm it's current, including GSLT token auth. No GPU dependency. Demand is smaller/niche vs. TF2 but stable long-tail community-server activity (SourceMod-extended player counts beyond the default 4). SERP is the same beatable Source-hosting crowd. Original L4D is not worth separate treatment — L4D2 supersedes it. Clean addition.

**Summary:** ADD — TF2, DayZ, L4D2. DO NOT ADD — WoW private servers (active 2026 Blizzard litigation/enforcement, business-level legal exposure), PUBG (no genuine open dedicated-server path exists — official partner-gated only, third-party "hosting" is misleading/nonfunctional).
